rubrics.criterion: After the patch, exactly one production module owns the per-instance concurrent invocation admission capability — parsing, validation, and defaulting of the boot-time cap setting, the in-flight and parked-request bookkeeping, admission, parking, resumption, and release — and no other production module re-implements any fragment of it locally.
rubrics.rationale: This case exists because that capability is hand-coded in pieces across request pipeline assembly, the shared state module, the signature wrappers, the socket-timeout middleware, and the entrypoint; the central obligation of the repair is a single owning implementation.

rubrics.criterion: With a valid positive cap configured at boot, the framework still limits concurrent user-function invocations on the instance to at most that number, and requests beyond the cap are held and admitted oldest-first as invocations settle.
rubrics.rationale: The gate's externally visible effect is the feature under rework; a consolidation that quietly disables or loosens the cap changes behavior rather than structure.

rubrics.criterion: Every termination path of an admitted invocation still releases its slot exactly once: normal completion, callback completion, thrown or rejected errors and the uncaught-error crash path, client disconnect, and socket inactivity timeout.
rubrics.rationale: In the case being refactored, release is the piece duplicated most widely; a real consolidation must keep all five termination paths correct without leaking or double-releasing a slot.

rubrics.criterion: Parsing, validation, and defaulting of the cap setting is defined in exactly one place, and both the request-admission path and the startup reporting consume that single definition instead of each parsing the raw setting.
rubrics.rationale: The case contains three independent parses of the same environment setting (request pipeline assembly plus two in the entrypoint); unifying them is a core outcome, and the repaired code must not let the request path and the startup path disagree about what counts as a usable value.

rubrics.criterion: No fragment of the admission capability remains hand-coded outside the single owning module for local use — for example a release copy kept in socket-event handling or in the signature wrappers' termination paths, an independent parse of the raw setting at startup, or bookkeeping state still defined in the shared cross-request state module.
rubrics.rationale: Partial consolidation is the most plausible failure mode for this instance: extracting the most visible piece (the request pipeline's gate) while leaving less visible duplicates (socket-event release copies, wrapper release calls, startup parses) would leave a conceptual change spread across several files.

rubrics.criterion: Every consumer of the gate — request pipeline assembly and middleware registration, the signature wrappers' callback-completion and crash paths, the socket-event handling in the timeout middleware, and the startup banner/validation — obtains admission behavior through the owning module's API rather than by importing and mutating shared mutable admission state defined elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: The scattered fragments coordinate through an exported mutable state object and duplicated local logic; routing the consumers through one API is the structural half of this repair and must be checked at every consumer site the case touches.

rubrics.criterion: Startup reporting still behaves as configured: the banner line reporting the concurrency level appears only when the setting is a valid positive integer, and a malformed or negative value produces exactly one startup error report naming the setting while the server still starts and serves.
rubrics.rationale: The entrypoint's validation and banner reads are among the fragmented locations in this case; the repair must keep their observable output correct even though they now consult the owner.

rubrics.criterion: Default behavior is not flipped: with the cap setting absent, no request is parked, queued, delayed, or refused, and no new log or banner output appears compared to the pre-capability behavior.
rubrics.rationale: This framework must stay fully concurrent when the platform setting is absent; a repair that leaves the gate half-armed in the unset case (for example, middleware always installed or a zero-cap interpreted as one) regresses the default deployment.

rubrics.criterion: The patch removes the fragments the consolidation makes obsolete: duplicated release helpers and inline release copies, redundant parses of the raw setting, marker-writing snippets in non-owner modules, and shared mutable admission state or interfaces no longer needed because the owner encapsulates them.
rubrics.rationale: The refactor's whole point is that the scattered copies stop existing; leaving superseded fragments in place would let them drift from the owner and defeat the rework even when behavior still looks right.

rubrics.criterion: The tree contains no debris from the old fragments: no commented-out copies of release or parsing logic, no orphaned helper functions, no unused exported state objects, no imports of removed symbols, and no unused type declarations left behind by the patch.
rubrics.rationale: In this case the superseded code is small and easy to overlook (a nine-line release routine, a two-field interface, a counter object); debris would keep the capability partially defined outside its owner and confuse the next maintainer.

rubrics.criterion: The repository builds and the full existing test suite passes without any existing test expectation having been modified, weakened, or deleted (adding new tests is acceptable).
rubrics.rationale: The case was built so that the entire pre-existing suite is green before and after the refactor; any need to edit existing expectations indicates an unintended behavior change, not a structural one.

rubrics.criterion: The pre-existing startup banner lines keep their exact wording and relative order, and the concurrency line is printed only under a valid positive cap.
rubrics.rationale: Operational tooling parses the framework's startup output; the refactor moves where the cap is read but must not disturb the existing banner contract.

rubrics.criterion: Unrelated request-handling behavior is not disturbed by the rework: status codes and payload handling for successful, error, and empty-result invocations, the crash-path response behavior, and the existing request timeout/abort machinery all behave as before.
rubrics.rationale: The case touches the wrapper and timeout modules, which also own crash responses and socket-timeout aborts; a plausible overreach in this repair is to alter those neighboring mechanisms while consolidating admission control.

rubrics.criterion: The admission accounting invariants hold even in paths the test suite does not exercise: a slot is never released twice for one request, a resumed request is not admitted while every slot is busy, parked requests resume in arrival order, and the in-flight count never goes negative or misses an admitted request.
rubrics.rationale: These invariants are invisible to the existing suite because the suite runs ungated, yet they are the framework's contract under the platform setting; subtle release ordering bugs here wed an instance at capacity exactly as the pre-refactor code risked doing.
